title: HTTP Caching: Speed Up Your Web Apps

scenes.say: Why do browsers cache files, and how does it actually work?

scenes.label: Cache
scenes.sub: Cache-Control sets rules for browser and CDN caching.
scenes.say: Cache-Control is the main header that sets rules for browser and CDN caching.

rows.b: Unique version ID for a resource

scenes.say: The big three headers: Cache-Control sets rules, ETag gives each resource a version, and Expires sets a hard expiry date.

scenes.title: Cache Headers in Action
scenes.say: Here’s a real example. Cache-Control tells the browser and CDN to cache for an hour. ETag marks the file version.

scenes.question: What does ETag do?
scenes.wrong: Sets how long to cache a file
scenes.right: It gives each file version a unique ID, so the server knows if the file changed.
scenes.say: Don’t mix these up: ETag doesn’t set cache time. It gives each file version a unique ID, so the server knows if it changed.
